Vidit enim in vultu et habitu Christi, quod esset valde veneranda persona, omni maturitate et probitate morum refulgens: ideo nominat eum Dominum. Nondum tamen putavit eum esse prophetam, vel Christum, aut Deum. Neque in quo haurias habes, id est, instrumentum hauriendi non habes ut ego, et puteus altus est, id est profundus: propter quod opus est hauritorio, quia cum manu nequit aqua educi. Frequenter in Scripturis ponitur altam pro profundo: ut Sapiens ait, Ab altitudine inferorum eduxit eos; et in Ecclesiastico, De altitudine ventris inferi liberasti me. Unde ergo habes aquam vivam, quam possis mihi præstare, si postularem? Et probat quod non possit, quia alium puteum vel fontem non possideret meliorem puteo isto.
paras.en: [[4:11|The woman saith to him|Dicit ei mulier]], who understood Christ's words of material water: [[4:11|Sir|Domine]]. For she saw in Christ's face and bearing that he was a person greatly to be revered, shining with all maturity and uprightness of manners: so she calls him Lord. Yet she did not yet think him to be a prophet, or the Christ, or God. [[4:11|thou hast nothing wherein to draw|neque in quo haurias habes]], that is, you have no vessel for drawing as I have, [[4:11|and the well is deep|et puteus altus est]], that is, profound, for which reason a drawing vessel is needed, since the water cannot be brought up by hand. In the Scriptures *altum* [“high”] is often put for *profundum* [“deep”]: as the Wise Man says, [[Wis 10:19|from the depth of hell she brought them out|Ab altitudine inferorum eduxit eos]]; and in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 51:7|From the depth of the belly of hell|De altitudine ventris inferi]] [Denis adds: “thou hast delivered me”] [the margin prints Eccli. li, 4, 7]. [[4:11|From whence then hast thou living water|Unde ergo habes aquam vivam]], which you could give me if I asked? And she proves that he could not, since he possessed no other well or fountain better than this well.

paras.t: Quod probat per hoc, quod non est major patriarcha Jacob. Numquid tu major es patre nostro Jacob? Reputabant enim Judæi et Samaritani, Abraham, Isaac et Jacob valde præcipuos exstitisse. Unde infra dicunt Judæi ad Christum: Numquid tu major es patre nostro Abraham? Qui dedit, id est, fossum reliquit, nobis puteum istum. Ex quo patet, quod fons de quo fuit jam sermo, puteus erat. Et ipse Jacob ex eo bibit, et filii ejus, et pecora ejus.
paras.en: This she proves from the fact that he is not greater than the patriarch Jacob: [[4:12|Art thou greater than our father Jacob|Numquid tu major es patre nostro Jacob]]? For the Jews and Samaritans held Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to have been of the very first rank. Hence below the Jews say to Christ: [[John 8:53|Art thou greater than our father Abraham|Numquid tu major es patre nostro Abraham]]? [[4:12|who gave us the well|qui dedit nobis puteum]] [Denis reads *puteum istum*, “this well”], that is, left it to us after digging it. From this it is plain that the fountain spoken of just now was a well[[4:6||]]. [[4:12|and drank thereof, himself and his children and his cattle?|Et ipse Jacob ex eo bibit, et filii ejus, et pecora ejus]].

paras.t: Respondit Jesus, et dixit ei: Omnis qui bibit ex aqua hac, et simili, sitiet iterum, si diu vixerit, et ad tempus competens a potu cessaverit. Qui autem biberit, id est, spiritualiter sumpserit, et mente gustaverit, ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, id est gratiam Spiritus Sancti, non sitiet in æternum. Hoc dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo sic: Non sitiet in «ternum: id est, licet ad tempus sitim spiritualem sustineat, suspirando ad patriam, eupiendoque gratiam perfectiorem atque aliorum saluitem; non tamen semper sic sitiet, sed veniet hora in qua replebitur bonis desiderium ejus, quia in die judicii in anima et corpore glorificabitur, et tune non deerit quod affectet hoc modo, ut scriptum est in Matthæo: Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur. Quando? Audi Psalmistam: Satiabor, ait, quum apparuerit gloria tua. — Secundo sic: Non sitiet in æternum, hoc est, nunquam sitiet appetendo rem omnino absentem nequaquam adeptam. Habet enim virtualiter omne bonum, quoniam gratiam habendo, habet Deum gratie fontem, et felicitatem æternam per inchoationem et continentiam virtualem. Nam gratia est inchoatio gloriæ, et virtualiter continet eam, sicut semen continet arborem. Juxta quem sensum ait Psalmista: Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum.
paras.en: [[4:13|Jesus answered and said to her: Whosoever drinketh of this water|Respondit Jesus, et dixit ei: Omnis qui bibit ex aqua hac]], and the like, [[4:13|shall thirst again|sitiet iterum]], if he lives long and for a fitting time leaves off drinking. [[4:13|but he that shall drink|Qui autem biberit]], that is, shall take spiritually and taste in his mind, [[4:13|of the water that I will give him|ex aqua quam ego dabo ei]], that is, the grace of the Holy Ghost, [[4:13|shall not thirst for ever|non sitiet in æternum]]. This can be understood in two ways. First thus: *shall not thirst for ever*: that is, though for a time he suffers spiritual thirst, sighing for the fatherland and longing for more perfect grace and for the salvation of others, yet he will not always thirst so; but the hour will come in which his desire will be filled with good things[[Ps 102:5||]], since on the day of judgment he will be glorified in soul and body, and then nothing he longs for will be lacking, in the way that is written in Matthew: [[Matt 5:6|Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill|Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur]]. When? Hear the Psalmist: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor, ait, quum apparuerit gloria tua]]. Secondly thus: *shall not thirst for ever*, that is, he will never thirst by desiring a thing wholly absent and in no way attained. For he has every good virtually, since in having grace he has God the fountain of grace, and eternal happiness by way of beginning and virtual containing. For grace is the beginning of glory and contains it virtually, as the seed contains the tree. In this sense the Psalmist says: [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum]].

paras.t: Sed his obviare videtur, quod in Ecclesiastico Christus Dei sapientia loquitur: Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient; e qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient. Dicendum quod secundum primam expositionem, istud nequaquam dissonat a prædictis; sed quantum ad secundam expositionem, videtur repugnantia quædam. Sciendum ergo, quod sitis in Scripturis tripliciter sumitur: Primo, pro desiderio rei nequaquam adeptæ: sicque acquisitio temporalium rerum generat sitim aliarum et plurium divitiarum, augendo cupiditatem. Secundo, pro desiderio rei adeptæ, ut habeatur magis perfecte: sicque sitit qui gratiam recipit, quoniam Deum et dona ejus qui habet imperfecte, desiderat perfectius possidere, pertingendo de fide et via ad speciem et patriam, emulanda quoque charismata meliora in præsenti, secundum doctrinam Apostoli. Tertio, pro amore rei præsentis, eum exclusione fastidii: sic Sancti in patria sitiunt Deum, quemadmodum Petrus ait de Christo: In quem desiderant angeli prospicere.
paras.en: But against this seems to be what Christ, the Wisdom of God, says in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 24:29|They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst|Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient ; e qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient]]. It must be said that by the first explanation this does not clash at all with what has been said; but as to the second explanation, there seems to be a certain contradiction. We must know, then, that thirst is taken in three ways in the Scriptures. First, for the desire of a thing not yet attained: and so the getting of temporal things breeds thirst for other and more riches, by increasing greed. Second, for the desire of a thing attained, that it may be had more perfectly: and so he thirsts who receives grace, since he who has God and his gifts imperfectly desires to possess them more perfectly, reaching from faith and the way to sight and the fatherland, and in this present life also being zealous for the better gifts, according to the Apostle's teaching[[1 Cor 12:31||]]. Third, for the love of a thing present, with the exclusion of weariness: so the Saints in the fatherland thirst for God, as Peter says of Christ: [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|In quem desiderant angeli prospicere]].

paras.t: Sed aqua, id est gratia gratum faciens, quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aqua, id est origo, formale principium atque meritoria ratio virtuosæ actionis, sancta contemplationis, ardentis desiderii, salientis, id est, animam ista terrena transilire facientis, pertingendo in vitam æternam. Quemadmodum enim natura est in nobis principium omnium naturalium operationum, sic gratia gratum faciens est fons intrinsecus atque principium omnium actionum meritoriarum, faciens ipsam essentiam rationalis creaturæ Deo acceptam, deiformem, Deo supernaturaliter copulatam, et ad promerendum supernaturalem felicitatem idoneam.
paras.en: [[4:14|But the water|Sed aqua]], that is, sanctifying grace, [[4:14|that I will give him shall become in him a fountain of water|quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ]], that is, the origin, the formal principle and the meritorious reason of virtuous action, of holy contemplation, of ardent desire, [[4:14|springing up|salientis]], that is, making the soul leap over these earthly things, reaching [[4:14|into life everlasting|in vitam æternam]]. For as nature is in us the principle of all natural operations, so sanctifying grace is the inward fountain and principle of all meritorious actions, making the very essence of the rational creature acceptable to God, godlike, supernaturally joined to God, and fit to merit supernatural happiness.

paras.t: Dicit ad eum mulier, verba hac mystica carnaliter intelligens (non enim erat solita audire hujusmodi): Domine, da mihi hanc aquam qua omnem sitim æternaliter aufert, videlicet aquam corporalem, de qua te loqui existimo, ut non sitiam corporaliter, neque veniam huc haurire. Propter duplex commodum petiit femina aquam talem: primo, ut a pœna sitis libera esset; secundo, ut a labore hauriendi eriperetur. Sic et nos spiritualem hanc aquam a Christo cordialiter jugiterque petamus, ut non sitiamus ista terrena, quee appetitum nequeunt satiare, sed quo eorum amore et occupatione homo magis involvitur, eo a divinorum conlemplatione, dilectione, et vera quiete ac libertate amplius impeditur ac elongatur; neque veniamus huc haurire, id est in exterioribus atque carnalibus consolationes viles requirere, sed in Domino sit tota delectatio nostra, et cum Jeremia dicere mereamur: Diem hominis non concupivi, tu scis. Qui enim cor suum ad exteriora effundit, qui humanas et sæculares delectationes admittit, nequaquam dignus est gustare quam dulcis est Dominus. Talis enim nunquam efficitur vere spiritualis, internus, et Deo suo familiaris atque carissimus.
paras.en: [[4:15|The woman said to him|Dicit ad eum mulier]], understanding these mystical words carnally (for she was not used to hearing such things): [[4:15|Sir, give me this water|Domine, da mihi hanc aquam]] which takes away all thirst for ever, namely bodily water, of which I think you are speaking, [[4:15|that I may not thirst|ut non sitiam]] bodily, [[4:15|nor come hither to draw|neque veniam huc haurire]]. The woman asked for such water for a twofold benefit: first, to be free of the pain of thirst; second, to be delivered from the labour of drawing. So let us too ask this spiritual water of Christ heartily and constantly, that we may not thirst for these earthly things, which cannot satisfy the appetite, but the more a man is wrapped up in love of them and busyness with them, the more he is hindered and kept far from the contemplation and love of divine things and from true rest and freedom; and that we may not come hither to draw, that is, seek cheap consolations in outward and carnal things, but that all our delight may be in the Lord, and that we may deserve to say with Jeremias: [[Jer 17:16|I have not desired the day of man, thou knowest|Diem hominis non concupivi, tu scis]]. For he who pours out his heart on outward things, who admits human and worldly delights, is in no way worthy to taste how sweet the Lord is[[Ps 33:9||]]. Such a man never becomes truly spiritual, inward, and familiar and very dear to his God.

paras.t: Denique, quoniam mulier ista verba Christi capere non valebat, incipit Christus eam inducere ad cognoscendum se ipsum, ut cognito ipso loquente, verba ejus seiantur esse spiritualia ac divina. Dicit ei Jesus: Vade, voca virum tuum, et veni huc simul eum illo. Quomodo dicit hoc Christus, qui est infallibilis veritas et sapientia Patris ? Noverat enim quod mulier ista virum proprie dictum, id est virum legitimum, non haberet. Sed hoc facile solvitur, ut sit sensus: Voca virum tuum, id est eum qui putatur esse maritus tuus legitimus, quamvis sit adulter. Sed numquid intentio Christi fuit ut mulier ista virum suum adduceret ? Quid enim ille fecisset adductus ? Si autem dicatur quod voluit Christus virum adduci, quatenus eum instrueret atque converteret, non infideliter dicitur. Si vero dicatur quod hoc non fuit intentio Christi, sed ut ex occasione hujus verbi et e» responsione mulieris, Christus eam convenientius argueret, respondebo quod si ait ad feminam hanc, Voca virum tuum, quomodo ait in Genesi Abrahæ, Tolle filium tuum unigenitum Isaac, et offer illum mihi in holocaustum: quod Dominus dixit, non ut sic fieret, sed ut tentaret: non quatenus ipse veritatem agnosceret. sed alii. Sic ergo nunc ait mulieri, Voca virum tuum.
paras.en: Then, since this woman could not grasp Christ's words, Christ begins to lead her on to know himself, so that, once the speaker is known, his words may be known to be spiritual and divine. [[4:16|Jesus saith to her: Go, call thy husband, and come hither|Dicit ei Jesus: Vade, voca virum tuum, et veni huc]] together with him. How does Christ say this, who is the infallible truth and the wisdom of the Father[[John 14:6||]][[1 Cor 1:24||]]? For he knew that this woman had no husband properly so called, that is, no lawful husband. But this is easily solved, the sense being: *call thy husband*, that is, him who is thought to be your lawful husband, though he is an adulterer. But was it Christ's intention that this woman should bring her husband? For what would he have done once brought? If it is said that Christ wished the man to be brought in order to instruct and convert him, that is not said unfaithfully. But if it is said that this was not Christ's intention, but that, taking occasion from this word and from the woman's answer, Christ might more fittingly reprove her, I shall answer that he said to this woman, *Call thy husband*, as he said in Genesis to Abraham: [[Gen 22:2|Take thy only begotten son Isaac|Tolle filium tuum unigenitum Isaac]] … [[Gen 22:2|thou shalt offer him for an holocaust|offer illum mihi in holocaustum]]: which the Lord said, not that it should be done so, but to try him; not so that he himself might come to know the truth, but others. So, then, he now says to the woman, *Call thy husband*.

paras.t: Respondit mulier, et dixit: Non habeo virum. Respondit ei Jesus: Bene, id est vere, dixisti, Quia non habeo virum, id est maritum legitimum. Quinque enim viros legitimos habuisti successive, et nunc quem habes modo, id est, qui jam putatur esse vir tuus legitimus, non est tuus vir. Hoc, videlicet, Non habeo virum, vere dixisti. Posset hic disputatio longa induci, quomodo intelligenda sint hac. Mulier equidem ista fuit eum adultero: quem tamen ipsa dixit esse suum maritum; et alii sic credebant, fuitque notorium in civitate Sichar, quod mulier hac fuit cum viro isto, ut communiter asserunt expositores. Dum ergo mulier dixit Christo. Non habeo virum, si per virum intellexit virum legitimum, publicavit proprium crimen quod intendebat abscondere; si vero per virum intellexit quemlibet masculum, negavit quod erat notorium. Non ergo Christus dixisset: Bene dixisti, Non habeo virum. Ad hoc respondendum videtur, quod mulier more adulterarum loquebatur sophistice, dicens, Non habeo virum, nomine viri intelligens virum legitimum: et ergo verum dicebat materialiter. Sed nomine viri voluit Jesum intelligere quemlibet masculum, ut ipsa continens crederetur: sicque mentiebatur formaliter, quoniam fallere satagebat, nee verebatur alieno veritatem abscondere, quem putavit secreta sua latere, moxque recedere.
paras.en: [[4:17|The woman answered and said: I have no husband|Respondit mulier, et dixit: Non habeo virum]]. Jesus answered her: [[4:17|Thou hast said well|Bene dixisti]], that is, truly, [[4:17|I have no husband|Quia non habeo virum]], that is, lawful husband. [[4:18|For thou hast had five husbands|Quinque enim viros legitimos habuisti]], lawful ones, one after another, [[4:18|and he whom thou now hast|et nunc quem habes]], that is, he who is now thought to be your lawful husband, [[4:18|is not thy husband|non est tuus vir]]. [[4:18|This, thou hast said truly|hoc vere dixisti]], namely, *I have no husband*. A long discussion could be brought in here on how these things are to be understood. This woman was in fact living with an adulterer, whom yet she said was her husband; and others believed so, and it was notorious in the city of Sichar that this woman was with this man, as the expositors commonly assert. When, then, the woman said to Christ, *I have no husband*, if by husband she understood a lawful husband, she made public her own crime, which she meant to hide; but if by husband she understood any male, she denied what was notorious. So Christ would not have said: *Thou hast said well, I have no husband*. To this it seems we must answer that the woman, after the manner of adulteresses, was speaking with sophistry, saying *I have no husband* and understanding by the name of husband a lawful husband: and so she spoke the truth materially [that is, the words themselves were true]. But by the name of husband she wished Jesus to understand any male, so that she might be believed continent; and so she lied formally [that is, in what she meant to convey], since she was trying to deceive, and was not afraid to hide the truth from a stranger, from whom she thought her secrets were hidden and who would soon go away.

paras.t: Dicit ei mulier: Domine, video, hoc est, ex revelatione secretorum meorum considero, quia propheta es tu. Sed quum prophetia sit de futuris contingentibus, quomodo sequebatur Christum esse prophetam, quia præterita et præsentia occulta cognovit? Dicendum, quod licet prophetia propriissime sumpta respiciat futurum contingens, est tamen, secundum Gregorium, etiam de præteritis et præsentibus divina revelatione patefactis.
paras.en: [[4:19|The woman saith to him: Sir, I perceive|Dicit ei mulier: Domine, video]], that is, from the revealing of my secrets I consider, [[4:19|that thou art a prophet|quia propheta es tu]]. But since prophecy is of future contingent things, how did it follow that Christ was a prophet because he knew hidden things past and present? It must be said that although prophecy taken most properly regards the future contingent, yet, according to Gregory, it is also of things past and present made known by divine revelation.

paras.t: Mulier ista nunc cœpit cognoscere excellentiam Christi, videlicet, quod esset propheta; sed nondum sciebat quod esset finis, impletor ac Dominus Prophetarum. Quoniam itaque vidit eum in divinis illuminatum, proponit sibi quæstionem, vel potius objicit sibi argumentum ad probandum errare Judæos, qui dixerunt quod in Jerusalem adorare oportet. Patres nostri, videlicet Jacob et filii ejus, et filii Israel egredientes ex /Ægypto, in monte hoc, id est in monte Garizim huie loco propinquo, adoraverunt, quando Jacob habitavit apud Sichem: quia in locis altis seu montibus orare et sacrificare solebant Judæi et patres eorum, templo nondum constructo, secundum quod Dominus dicit ad Abraham: Tolle Isaac, et offer illum mihi super unum montium quem monstravero tibi. Sed et sex tribus israel stabant in monte Garizim ad benedicendum, et aliæ sex in monte Hebal ad maledicendum, quemadmodum in Deuteronomio jusserat Dominus.
paras.en: This woman now began to know the excellence of Christ, namely that he was a prophet; but she did not yet know that he was the end, the fulfiller and the Lord of the Prophets. Since, then, she saw him enlightened in divine things, she puts a question to him, or rather puts to him an argument to prove that the Jews were in error, who said that [[4:20|at Jerusalem is the place where men must adore|Jerosolymis est locus ubi adorare oportet]]. [[4:20|Our fathers|Patres nostri]], namely Jacob and his sons, and the children of Israel going out of Egypt, [[4:20|adored on this mountain|in monte hoc adoraverunt]], that is, on Mount Garizim, near this place, when Jacob dwelt at Sichem: for the Jews and their fathers were wont to pray and sacrifice in high places or on mountains before the temple was built, according to what the Lord says to Abraham: [[Gen 22:2|thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee|offer illum mihi super unum montium quem monstravero tibi]] [Denis: “Take Isaac, and offer him to me upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee”]. And six tribes of Israel stood on Mount Garizim to bless, and the other six on Mount Hebal to curse, as the Lord had commanded in Deuteronomy[[Deut 27:12||]][[Deut 27:13||]].

paras.t: Sed quomodo mulier ista nominat sanctos Patriarchas patres suos, quum non esset de semine illorum progenita ? Samaritani quippe fuerunt natione gentiles, D) quia Salmanasar rex Assyriorum, decem tribubus partim occisis, partimque captis ac translatis, posuit Medos in terra decem tribuum. Qui quum devorarentur a leonibus, eo quod Deum Israel non colebant, misit eis rex Assyriorum unum de sacerdotibus populi Israel, ut doceret eos legitima Dei terræ Israel: quo facto, cœperunt colere Dominum; recipientes dumtaxat quinque libros Moysis, et idola sua non relinquentes, prout in libris Regum plenius recitatur. Dicendum, quod mulier vocat illos suos seu Samaritanorum paires, quia Samaritani sequebantur cultum et ritum illorum in multis, et propter reverentiam Patriarcharum.
paras.en: But how does this woman call the holy Patriarchs her fathers, when she was not born of their seed? For the Samaritans were Gentiles by nation, since Salmanasar king of the Assyrians, when the ten tribes had been partly slain and partly taken captive and carried away[[4 Kings 17:6||]], placed Medes in the land of the ten tribes[[4 Kings 17:24||]]. When these were being devoured by lions because they did not worship the God of Israel, the king of the Assyrians sent them one of the priests of the people of Israel to teach them the ordinances of the God of the land of Israel[[4 Kings 17:25||]]; this done, they began to worship the Lord, accepting only the five books of Moses and not giving up their idols[[4 Kings 17:29||]], as is told more fully in the books of Kings. It must be said that the woman calls them her fathers, or the Samaritans' fathers, because the Samaritans followed their worship and rite in many things, and out of reverence for the Patriarchs.

paras.t: Et vos Judæi dicitis, quia Jerosolymis est locus, hoc est templum in monte Sion, ubi adorare oportet, id est, expeditius est quam in monte Garizim. Judæi autem non dixerunt quod oporteret de necessitate adorare in templo Jerusalem, quasi Deus alibi non exaudiret: nam in synagogis suis orare consueverunt. Sed asserebant convenientiorem locum orandi esse in Jerusalem: quod et verum fuit, quoniam Deus specialiter elegit locum illum pro cultu suo, præsertim ad sacrificandum.
paras.en: [[4:20|and you say|Et vos Judæi dicitis]], you Jews, [[4:20|that at Jerusalem is the place|quia Jerosolymis est locus]], that is, the temple on Mount Sion, [[4:20|where men must adore|ubi adorare oportet]], that is, where it is more fitting than on Mount Garizim. Now the Jews did not say that one must of necessity adore in the temple at Jerusalem, as though God would not hear elsewhere: for they were accustomed to pray in their synagogues. But they held that the more fitting place of prayer was at Jerusalem: and that was true, since God specially chose that place for his worship[[Deut 12:5||]], above all for sacrifice.

paras.t: Dicit ei Jesus: Mulier, crede mihi, quem vides esse prophetam. Nisi enim credideritis, non intelligetis. Et accedentem ad Deum necesse est credere. Quia veniet hora quando neque in monte hoc Garizim, æque in Jerosolymis adorabitis Patrem. Hoc intelligi potest dupliciter: Primo, quod conversi ad Christum non adorarent Patrem cecelestem in prædictis locis, eo modo quo ante, videlicet æstimando quod determinatio et distinctio locorum tam multum prodessent ad effectum orationis obtinendum; sed spirituales effecti, spiritualiter adorarent, scientes quod virtus et valor orationis non principaliter consistit in loco, sed animo. Secundo sic: Veniet hora, etc., quod im pletum videtur tempore destructionis Jerusalem a Romanis, quia et tune plurimi Samaritani crediderunt in Christum, atque in ecclesiis adorare curabant.
paras.en: [[4:21|Jesus saith to her: Woman, believe me|Dicit ei Jesus: Mulier, crede mihi]], whom you see to be a prophet. For *unless you believe, you will not understand*[[Is 7:9||]] [the margin gives Is. vii, 9, according to the Septuagint; the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have “If you will not believe, you shall not continue”]. And [[Heb 11:6|he that cometh to God must believe|accedentem ad Deum necesse est credere]]. [[4:21|that the hour cometh, when you shall neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, adore the Father|Quia veniet hora quando neque in monte hoc Garizim, æque in Jerosolymis adorabitis Patrem]] [Denis reads *veniet*, “shall come”]. This can be understood in two ways. First, that those converted to Christ would not adore the heavenly Father in these places in the way they did before, namely judging that the fixing and distinguishing of places did so much good towards obtaining the effect of prayer; but, become spiritual, they would adore spiritually, knowing that the power and worth of prayer does not consist chiefly in the place, but in the mind. Second thus: *the hour cometh*, etc., which seems to have been fulfilled at the time of the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans, since then also very many Samaritans believed in Christ, and took care to adore in churches.

paras.t: Vos Samaritani adoratis quod nescitis. Adorabant enim Deum omnium creatorem, quem nesciebant, id est, male et false de ipso senserunt, putantes Deum esse corporeum, cireumscriptum, et lineamentis corporalibus figuratum. Adora bant quoque et idola qui nescierunt, putantes aliquid divinitatis illis inesse, qua plena fuerunt dæmoniis. Vos Judæi ado ramus quod scimus, id est Deum, quem vere eognoseimus. Christus cognovit eum per speciem, ceteri per fidem. Notus enim in Judæa Deus. Ceteris enim nationibus ad diversos errores ruentibus, remansit in populo [Israelitico vera cognitio Dei. Quia salus ex Judæis est, hoc est, ex populo Judæorum Salvator mundi incarnatus et ortus est; vel, Salus ex Judæis est, hoc est, salvatio gentium ex Judæis dependet, puta a Christi passione et Apostolorum prædicatione.
paras.en: [[4:22|You adore that which you know not|Vos Samaritani adoratís quod nescitis]], you Samaritans. For they adored God the creator of all, whom they did not know, that is, they thought ill and falsely of him, supposing God to be bodily, circumscribed, and shaped with bodily features. They adored idols also, not knowing, thinking that something of divinity was in them, though they were full of demons. [[4:22|we adore that which we know|nos adoramus quod scimus]], we Jews, that is, God, whom we truly know. Christ knew him by sight, the rest by faith. For [[Ps 75:2|In Judea God is known|Notus enim in Judæa Deus]]: while the other nations rushed into divers errors, the true knowledge of God remained in the Israelite people. [[4:22|For salvation is of the Jews|Quia salus ex Judæis est]], that is, from the people of the Jews the Saviour of the world was made flesh and born; or, *salvation is of the Jews*, that is, the salvation of the Gentiles depends on the Jews, namely on Christ's passion and the preaching of the Apostles.

paras.t: Sed venit hora, et nunc est, videlicet tempus evangelicæ legis, quando veri, hoc est fideles, sinceri atque devoti adoratores adorabunt Patrem, id est Deum trinum ac simplicem, cui dicimus: Pater noster qui es in cœlis, in spiritu, hoc est corde interno, in spirituali intellectu, in Spiritu Sancto, non solum in locis determinatis, in grossa imaginatione, in proprio sensu; et veritate, id est fide illuminata, in vera justitia, ad Dei honorem, et propter veram beatitudinem adipiscendam. Denique, secundum Augustinum, Patrem in veritate adorat, qui Patrem «æternum in nomine Filii invocat. Hoc est Deum veraciter invocare, id est intus et ex corde vocare. Quod quam salubre sit, pandit Psalmista dicendo: Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate.
paras.en: [[4:23|But the hour cometh and now is|Sed venit hora, et nunc est]], namely the time of the law of the Gospel, [[4:23|when the true adorers|quando veri adoratores]], that is, the faithful, sincere and devout, [[4:23|shall adore the Father|adorabunt Patrem]], that is, God three and simple, to whom we say: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster qui es in cœlis]], [[4:23|in spirit|in spiritu]], that is, with the inward heart, in spiritual understanding, in the Holy Ghost, not only in fixed places, in gross imagination, in one's own sense; [[4:23|and in truth|et veritate]], that is, with enlightened faith, in true justice, for God's honour, and in order to gain true beatitude. Further, according to Augustine, he adores the Father in truth who calls upon the eternal Father in the name of the Son. This is to call upon God truly, that is, to call inwardly and from the heart. How wholesome this is the Psalmist makes plain, saying: [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him|Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum]] [[Ps 144:18|in truth|in veritate]].

paras.t: Nam et Pater cœlestis tales quærit, id est, veros adoratores requirit et approbat: vult enim nos esse tales; qui adorent eum in spiritu et veritate, ut dictum est. Cujus ratio subditur: Spiritus est Deus, id est spiritualis, incorporalis et simplex essentia, utpote actus purus. Mens separata esset tantum honoratissimus intellectus. Et eos qui adorant eum adoratione latriæ, qua soli Deo debetur, in spiritu et veritate (secundum sensum inductum) oportet adorare, si debeant exaudiri. Actio quippe rationalis creatura per hoc complacet Deo, quod per eam assimilatur atque unitur suo Creatori. Per adorationem autem in spiritu et veritate factam, assimilatur et conjungitur Deo. Per hanc enim simplificatur, et recte ascendit in Deum, transcendendo cuncta terrena omnesque distractiones, et se ipsam pure elevando in Creatorem. Unde oratio dicitur ascensus mentis in Deum. Quasi dicat Salvator: Si Deus localis, corporalis ma terialisve esset in propria natura, adorandus esset in delerminatis locis dumtaxat et rudibus phantasiis. Nunc vero, quum sit spiritus simplicissimus, in interiori adorandus est templo, ut anima redeat ac se ipsam, et collecta atque in Deum forti stabilitate erecta, invocet Deum: quem. admodum in Ecclesiastico legitur, Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum. Hine dicit Apostolus: Si orem lingua, mens mea sine fructu est. Quid ergo? Orabo spiritu, orabo et mente.
paras.en: [[4:23|For the Father also seeketh such|Nam et Pater cœlestis tales quærit]], the heavenly Father, that is, seeks and approves true adorers, for he wills us to be such, [[4:23|to adore him|qui adorent eum]] in spirit and in truth, as has been said. The reason of this is added: [[4:24|God is a spirit|Spiritus est Deus]], that is, a spiritual, incorporeal and simple essence, namely pure act. A separated mind would be only a most honoured intellect. [[4:24|and they that adore him|Et eos qui adorant eum]] with the adoration of *latria* [that is, the worship due to God alone], which is due to God alone, [[4:24|must adore him in spirit and in truth|in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare]] (in the sense given), if they are to be heard. For the action of a rational creature pleases God in this, that by it the creature is made like to its Creator and united with him. And by adoration made in spirit and truth it is made like to God and joined to him: for by it it is made simple, and rises straight to God, passing beyond all earthly things and all distractions, and lifting itself up purely to the Creator. Hence prayer is called the ascent of the mind to God. As though the Saviour said: If God were local, bodily or material in his own nature, he would have to be adored only in fixed places and with rude imaginings. But now, since he is a most simple spirit, he must be adored in the inner temple, so that the soul returns to itself, and, gathered and raised up to God in strong steadiness, calls upon God: as we read in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 18:23|Before prayer prepare thy soul: and be not as a man that tempteth God|Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 14:14|if I pray in a tongue|Si orem lingua]], [[1 Cor 14:14|my understanding is without fruit|mens mea sine fructu est]]. [[1 Cor 14:15|What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the understanding|Quid ergo? Orabo spiritu, orabo et mente]].

paras.t: Itaque non vaga et huc illucque discurrente mente, imploranda est gratia Dei sed omni custodia custodiat orans cor suum, occasiones evagationum vitando, e cum fervore incipiendo. Quod non est modice laboriosum, secundum quod abbas Agathon dixit: Non est labor sicut orare Deum.
paras.en: So the grace of God is not to be implored with a wandering mind that runs hither and thither, but the one who prays should keep his heart with all watchfulness[[Prov 4:23||]], avoiding the occasions of wandering, and beginning with fervour. This is no small labour, according to what Abbot Agathon said: There is no labour like praying to God.

paras.t: Porro Salvator dicendo, Veri adoratores, etc., innuit esse quosdam adoratores falsos, videlicet, qui vel male sentiunt de Deo, sicut hæretici; vel propter humana præconia seu carnalia commoda aut temporalia lucra orant, sicut hypocritæ; vel Deum quem orando honorare videntur, pessimis moribus inhonorant. De quibus Deus ait per Isaiam: Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me; propter quod in vanum colunt me. Isti non exaudiuntur. Qui enim declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis.
paras.en: Further, the Saviour, by saying *the true adorers*, etc., implies that there are some false adorers: namely those who either think ill of God, as heretics do; or pray for human praise or carnal advantages or temporal gain, as hypocrites do; or dishonour by their wicked manners the God whom by praying they seem to honour. Of whom God says through Isaias[[Is 29:13||]]: [[Mark 7:6|This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me|Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me]]; [[Mark 7:7|And in vain do they worship me|in vanum colunt me]] [Denis: “therefore in vain do they worship me”; he gives Isaias's words in the form the Gospel quotes them]. These are not heard. For [[Prov 28:9|He that turneth away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination|Qui … declinat aurem suam … exsecrabilis]].

paras.t: Dicit ei mulier: Scio ex communi fama vel auctoritate Scripturæ, quia Messias venit, id est, mox venturus est, qui dicitur Christus. Samaritani namque noverant ut in Genesi prædictum est: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femoribus ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium. Quoniam ergo viderunt jam regnum a semine Judæ ablatum atque Herodi Ascalonitæ alienigenæ datum, poterant scire quod tempus adventus Messiæ instaret. Et hoc erat tunc publica fama apud Judæos. Unde miserunt ad Joannem scisceitantes an esset Christus. Quum ergo venerit ille, nobis annuntiabit omnia, id est, certficabit nos de quæstionibus universis, et ceteris ad salutem spectantibus: quasi diceret mulier ista, Tunc plenius instruemur de omnibus istis. Omnes autem Judi et ceteri de Christo aliquid loqui scientes, exspectabant eum quasi sapientissimum magistrum, summumque Prophetam.
paras.en: [[4:25|The woman saith to him: I know|Dicit ei mulier: Scio]], from common report or from the authority of Scripture, [[4:25|that the Messias cometh|quia Messias venit]], that is, is soon to come, [[4:25|who is called Christ|qui dicitur Christus]]. For the Samaritans knew what was foretold in Genesis: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femoribus ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium]]. Since, then, they now saw the kingdom taken from the seed of Juda and given to Herod the Ascalonite, a foreigner, they could know that the time of the coming of the Messias was at hand. And this was then a common report among the Jews. Hence they sent to John, asking whether he was the Christ[[John 1:19||]]. [[4:25|therefore, when he is come, he will tell us all things|Quum ergo venerit ille, nobis annuntiabit omnia]], that is, will make us certain about all questions and the other things that bear on salvation: as though this woman said, Then we shall be more fully instructed about all these things. For all the Jews, and the others who knew how to speak anything of Christ, awaited him as a most wise master and the highest Prophet.

paras.t: Dicit ei Jesus, Dominus inæstimabilis dignationis: Ego sum Christus qui loquor tecum. Quoniam enim Jesus vidit hanc feminam de cognitione divinorum sollicitam, revelavit ei se ipsum.
paras.en: [[4:26|Jesus saith to her|Dicit ei Jesus]], the Lord of inestimable condescension: [[4:26|I am he, who am speaking with thee|Ego sum Christus qui loquor tecum]] [Denis: “I am the Christ, who speak with thee”]. For since Jesus saw this woman anxious for the knowledge of divine things, he revealed himself to her.

paras.t: Et continuo venerunt discipuli ejus, redeuntes de civitate Sichar, in qua emerant escas, ut venientes, manducarent cum Jesu supra puteum, ut opinor, prout solent pauperes facere; e? mirabantur quia cum muliere loquebatur. Nihil mali suspicabantur; sed mirabantur, vel magnitudinem dignationis Christi, quod cum muliere. infideli tam familiariter conferebat, vel quia consuetudinem loquendi cum mulieribus seorsum ac privatim non habebat. Nemo tamen. ex discipulis dixit Christo: Quid quæris, aut quid loqueris cum ea. Propter reverentiam enim magistri sui nil tale dixerunt, certi quod non sine ratione affatus fuit hanc feminam.
paras.en: [[4:27|And immediately his disciples came|Et continuo venerunt discipuli ejus]], coming back from the city of Sichar, where they had bought food, so that on arriving they might eat with Jesus at the well, I suppose, as poor people are wont to do; [[4:27|And they wondered that he talked with the woman|et mirabantur quia cum muliere loquebatur]]. They suspected nothing evil; but they wondered either at the greatness of Christ's condescension, that he conversed so familiarly with an unbelieving woman, or because he did not have the custom of speaking with women apart and privately. [[4:27|Yet no man said|Nemo tamen. ex discipulis dixit]] of the disciples to Christ: [[4:27|What seekest thou? Or: Why talkest thou with her|Quid quæris, aut quid loqueris cum ea]]. For out of reverence for their master they said nothing of the kind, certain that he had not spoken to this woman without reason.

paras.t: Reliquit ergo hydriam suam mulier ad puteum. Pre admiratione enim eorum qua audivit, et dilectione quam concepit ad Christum, qui eam tam dignanter ac dulciter fuerat allocutus, quod Judæi non fecissent, pre desiderio quoque salutis populi sui, oblita est aquam corporalem secum deferre, aqua sapientiæ degustata. Et abiit in civitatem Sichar, et dicit illis hominibus suis concivibus: Venite, et videte hominem qui dixit mihi omnia quæcumque feci, hoc est opera mea præcipua. Vel mulier dicit hoc per hyperbolen seu excessum, ad innuendum quod Christus dixit sibi multa occulta de suo statu. Homines enim in admiratione magna positi et amore accensi, frequenter per excessum loquuntur, non intendentes aliquid falsi asserere, sed rei magnitudinem aperire. Numquid ipse est Christus? tanquam dicat: Videtur per tantum miraculum, quod sic.
paras.en: [[4:28|The woman therefore left her waterpot|Reliquit ergo hydriam suam mulier]] at the well. For out of wonder at what she had heard, and the love she had conceived for Christ, who had spoken to her so graciously and sweetly, which the Jews would not have done, and out of longing too for the salvation of her people, she forgot to carry the bodily water with her, having tasted the water of wisdom. [[4:28|and went her way into the city|Et abiit in civitatem]] of Sichar, [[4:28|and saith to the men there|et dicit illis hominibus]], her fellow-citizens: [[4:29|Come, and see a man who has told me all things whatsoever I have done|Venite, et videte hominem qui dixit mihi omnia quæcumque feci]], that is, my chief deeds. Or the woman says this by hyperbole or overstatement, to suggest that Christ had told her many hidden things about her state. For men placed in great wonder and on fire with love often speak with overstatement, not meaning to assert anything false, but to lay open the greatness of the thing. [[4:29|Is not he the Christ|Numquid ipse est Christus]]? as though she said: By so great a miracle it seems that he is.

paras.t: Mulier ista implevit quod admonet Petrus, dicendo, Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes; et talentum sibi concessum studuit fructuose expendere. Ad litteram quoque reliquit hydriam suam, quia intendebat statim reverti et plenius informari. Sic et nos dum illuminationem et gratiam Christi experimur, hydriam nostram, id est ventris curam, voluptatem omnemque terrenam substantiam, parvi pendere vel abjeetare debemus, aliosque ad similem gratiam pro posse adducere. Unicuique enim mandavit Deus de proximo suo quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico legitur.
paras.en: This woman fulfilled what Peter admonishes, saying: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]; and she was eager to lay out fruitfully the talent granted her. Literally too she left her waterpot, because she meant to come back at once and be more fully informed. So we too, when we experience the enlightenment and grace of Christ, ought to think little of our waterpot, that is, the care of the belly, pleasure and all earthly substance, or to cast it away, and to bring others to a like grace as far as we can. [[Ecclus 17:12|And he gave to every one of them commandment concerning his neighbour|Unicuique enim mandavit Deus de proximo suo]] [Denis: “For God hath given to every one commandment concerning his neighbour”], as we read in Ecclesiasticus.

paras.t: Et exierunt de civitate habitatores ejus novitate rei permoti, et ad credendum dis positi; et venerunt ad eum. Sic et nos sa lutaribus exhortationibus acquiescere par est, quoniam egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam, ut scribitur in Proverbiis.
paras.en: [[4:30|They went therefore out of the city|Et exierunt de civitate]], its inhabitants, moved by the newness of the thing and disposed to believe; [[4:30|and came unto him|et venerunt ad eum]]. So it is right for us too to give way to wholesome exhortations, since [[Prov 13:18|Poverty and shame to him that refuseth instruction|egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam]], as is written in Proverbs.

paras.t: Interea, id est inter hæc, utpote inter recessum mulieris et Samaritanorum accessum, rogabant eum discipuli ejus di. centes: Rabbi, manduca. Compatiebantur enim fatigationi sui magistri,. et proprie fami consulere quæsierunt. Ipsi nam quæ esuriebant, et quia non præsumebant comedere nisi magistro jubente, incipiente, et escam benedicente, idcirco rogabant ut manducaret. Ille autem dixit eis: Ego cibum habeo manducare, id. est spirituali alimonia animam meam reficere, scilicet opere virtuoso, quod mentem alit atque delectat, quemadmodum scriptum est, Cibabit illum pane vite et intellectus; quem vos nescitis, qui nondum cognoscitis mysteria mea.
paras.en: [[4:31|In the mean time|Interea]], that is, between these things, namely between the woman's going away and the Samaritans' coming, [[4:31|the disciples prayed him, saying: Rabbi, eat|rogabant eum discipuli, dicentes: Rabbi, manduca]]. For they felt for their master's weariness, and sought to provide for their own hunger. For they themselves were hungry, and since they did not presume to eat unless their master bade them, began, and blessed the food, they therefore asked him to eat. [[4:32|But he said to them: I have meat to eat|Ille autem dixit eis: Ego cibum habeo manducare]], that is, to refresh my soul with spiritual nourishment, namely with virtuous work, which feeds and delights the mind, as it is written: [[Ecclus 15:3|With the bread of life and understanding, she shall feed him|Cibabit illum pane vitæ et intellectus]]; [[4:32|which you know not|quem vos nescitis]], who do not yet know my mysteries.

paras.t: Dicebant ergo discipuli, verba magistri de materiali cibo intelligentes, ad invicem, quia ex reverentia quam habebant ad magistrum suum, non audebant faciliter alloqui eum: Numquid aliquis attulit ei manducare? Noverant siquidem quod nihil alimenti attulit secum. Non mirum quod mulier non intellexit verba Christi de aqua, quum discipuli non intellexerint verba ejus de esca.
paras.en: [[4:33|The disciples therefore said one to another|Dicebant ergo discipuli ad invicem]], understanding their master's words of bodily food (to one another, because out of the reverence they had for their master they did not dare speak to him readily): [[4:33|Hath any man brought him to eat|Numquid aliquis attulit ei manducare]]? For they knew that he had brought no food with him. No wonder that the woman did not understand Christ's words about water, when the disciples did not understand his words about food.

paras.t: Dicit eis Jesus, se ipsum exponens plane et cito, non per ambages atque circuitum quo locutus fuit, ad feminam. Discipulis enim tanquam familiaribus, patefecit mysteria; ceteris tanquam extraneis, loquebatur obscurius. Meus cibus præcipuus, id est in quo magis quam in corporali cibo delector et reereor, est ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me, id est facere opera Deo Patri placentia, ut perficiam opus ejus singulare et maximum, id est, hominum conversioni intendam, atque humani generis liberationem consummem. De quo opere ait infra Salvator: Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem. Hie docuit nos Christus suo exemplo, ut spiritualem refectionem aliorum proprie corporali refectioni præferamus, potiusque escam cordis quam corporis requiramus.
paras.en: [[4:34|Jesus saith to them|Dicit eis Jesus]], explaining himself plainly and quickly, not with the windings and the roundabout way in which he spoke to the woman. For to the disciples, as to his intimates, he laid open his mysteries; to the others, as to outsiders, he spoke more obscurely. [[4:34|My meat is|Meus cibus præcipuus, id est]] chiefly, that is, the thing in which I delight and am refreshed more than in bodily food, [[4:34|to do the will of him that sent me|ut faciam voluntatem ejus qui misit me]], that is, to do works pleasing to God the Father, [[4:34|that I may perfect his work|ut perficiam opus ejus]], his singular and greatest work, that is, that I may give myself to the conversion of men, and accomplish the deliverance of the human race. Of this work the Saviour says below: [[John 17:4|I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do|Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem]]. Here Christ taught us by his example to put the spiritual refreshment of others before our own bodily refreshment, and to seek the food of the heart rather than of the body.

paras.t: Loquitur autem Scriptura de cibo multiplici, utpote: de cibo seu pane Beatorum regnantium, qui est ipsa Divinitas vel ejus fruitio, qua duleissime atque firmissime sustentantur comprehensores. Unde in Luca loquitur Christus discipulis: Ego dispono vobis sicut disposuit mihi Pater, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno. Et alibi scriptum est: Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno Dei. Secundo, de cibo sacramentali, juxta illud: Caro mea vere est cibus. Tertio, de cibo interne compunctionis, ut est illud, Fuerunt mihi lacrima mes panes die ac nocte; itemque, Cibabis nos pane lacrimarum. Quarto, de pane bonæ æc meritori? operationis, ut habetur in Ecclesiastico: Ante obitum tuum operare justitiam quoniam non est apud inferos invenire cibos. Quinto, de pane corporalis refectionis.
paras.en: Scripture speaks of food in many senses: namely, of the food or bread of the Blessed who reign, which is the Godhead itself or the enjoyment of it, by which those who have attained [*comprehensores*, the blessed in heaven, as opposed to *viatores*, those still on the way] are most sweetly and most firmly sustained. Hence in Luke Christ says to the disciples: [[Luke 22:29|And I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me|Ego dispono vobis sicut disposuit mihi Pater]], [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno]]. And elsewhere it is written: [[Luke 14:15|Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God|Beatus qui manducabit panem in regno Dei]] [the margin prints Ibid. xiv, 15, that is, Luke]. Second, of sacramental food, according to that: [[John 6:56|For my flesh is meat indeed|Caro mea vere est cibus]]. Third, of the food of inward compunction, as is that: [[Ps 41:4|My tears have been my bread day and night|Fuerunt mihi lacrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte]]; and again, [[Ps 79:6|feed us with the bread of tears|Cibabis nos pane lacrimarum]]. Fourth, of the bread of good and meritorious work, as is had in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 14:17|Before thy death work justice: for in hell there is no finding food|Ante obitum tuum operare justitiam quoniam non est apud inferos invenire cibos]]. Fifth, of the bread of bodily refreshment.

paras.t: Deinde ostendit Christus per simile quod jam adfuit tempus prædictæ opera tionis, videlicet conversionis hominum Nonne vos dicitis quod adhuc quatuoi menses lunares, quibus utuntur Judæi ir computando, sunt, id est, restant, et mes sis venit, id est, antequam corporalis usualisque messis seu frugum collectio im: pleatur? Ecce dico vobis: Levate oculos vestros, et videte regiones, quia jam albæ sunt ad messem. Si adhuc quatuor men: ses restabant ad messem, palam quod verba ista non possint de corporali messe intelligi. Est igitur sensus: Levate oculos vestros mentales, id est, corda conside rando erigite, et videte regiones, id est habitatores terræ interiori visu adspicite quia jam albæ sunt ad messem, id est tempus est ut congregentur in horreum meum, et perducantur ad fidem: nun enim venit tempus miserationis et gra ti&. Potest autem specialiter referri ad Samaritanos Christo propinquantes, qui dispositi erant ad fidei receptionem. Quasi dicat Salvator: Istos Samaritanos cunctos quæ peccatores oculo compassionis adspi. cite, et magis curate ut eorum conversion quam corporali comestioni intendam.
paras.en: Next Christ shows by a likeness that the time of the said work, namely the conversion of men, had already come. [[4:35|Do not you say: There are yet four months|Nonne vos dicitis quod adhuc quatuor menses]], lunar months, which the Jews use in reckoning, [[4:35|and then the harvest cometh|sunt, et messis venit?]], that is, *are*, remain, before the bodily and usual harvest or gathering of crops is completed? [[4:35|Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the countries. For they are white already to harvest|Ecce díco vobis : Levate oculos vestros, et videte regiones, quia jam albæ sunt ad messem]]. If four months still remained to the harvest, it is plain that these words cannot be understood of the bodily harvest. The sense therefore is: *Lift up your eyes* of the mind, that is, raise up your hearts by considering, *and see the countries*, that is, look with inward sight on the inhabitants of the earth, *for they are white already to harvest*, that is, it is time for them to be gathered into my barn and brought to the faith: for now the time of mercy and grace has come. It can also be referred especially to the Samaritans drawing near to Christ, who were disposed to receive the faith. As though the Saviour said: Look on these Samaritans and all sinners with the eye of compassion, and care rather that I attend to their conversion than to bodily eating.

paras.t: Dicitur vero collectio hominum messis per similitudinem. Quemadmodum enim in messe colliguntur fructus terra in aream, sic electi congregantur intra Ecclesiam. Insuper advertendum, quod Scriptura loquitur de duplici messe spirituali: Una qua homines spiritualiter congregantur per fidem et gratiam intra Ecclesiam militantem. Unde in Matthæo habetur: Rogate Dominum messis ut mittat operarios in messem suam. Alia est messis qua electi colliguntur per gloriosam resurrectionem intra Ecclesiam triumphantem ad patriam: de qua ait Christus in Matthæo Messores sunt angeli, messis vero consummatio mundi.
paras.en: The gathering of men is called a harvest by likeness. For as in harvest the fruits of the earth are gathered into the threshing-floor, so the elect are gathered within the Church. Besides, it is to be noted that Scripture speaks of a twofold spiritual harvest: one in which men are spiritually gathered by faith and grace within the Church militant; hence in Matthew it is had: [[Matt 9:38|Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth labourers into his harvest|Rogate Dominum messis ut mittat operarios in messem suam]]. The other is the harvest in which the elect are gathered by the glorious resurrection within the Church triumphant in the fatherland; of which Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 13:39|And the reapers are the angels|Messores sunt angeli]] … [[Matt 13:39|But the harvest is the end of the world|messis vero consummatio mundi]].

paras.t: Deinceps subditur de mercede messorum prima messis, videlicet de præmio doctorum et prædicatorum. Et qui metit, hoc est, falce seu verbo prædicationis homines ad fidem gratiamque inducit, mercedem accipit, utpote gloriam regni cœlestis, premium essentiale, quod est visio Dei, atque aureolam qua martyribus, virginibus et doctoribus est promissa; et congregat fructum, hoc est spirituales filios sua. prædicatione conversos, in vitam æternam, quia ad eam finaliter dirigit eos.
paras.en: Then there is added, of the wages of the reapers of the first harvest, namely of the reward of doctors and preachers: [[4:36|And he that reapeth|Et qui metit]], that is, leads men to faith and grace with the sickle or word of preaching, [[4:36|receiveth wages|mercedem accipit]], namely the glory of the heavenly kingdom, the essential reward, which is the vision of God, and the aureole [that is, the special added crown of joy] promised to martyrs, virgins and doctors; [[4:36|and gathereth fruit|et congregat fructum]], that is, spiritual children converted by his preaching, [[4:36|unto life everlasting|in vitam æternam]], since he directs them to it in the end.

paras.t: Vel, Congregat fructum, hoc est meritum copiosum pertingens in vitam æternam, quia est finis et premium. Omnium quippe divinarum perfectionum altissima, est Dei cooperatorem exsistere in reductione hominum ad suum principium finemque ultimum, secundum Dionysium. De quorum premio scriptum est in Daniele: Qui multos erudiunt ad justitiam, fulgebunt quasi stellæ in perpetuas :æternitates. Ut et qui seminat, id est chorus sanctorum Patriarcharum et veterum Prophetarum, qui primo ecperunt verbum Dei in cordibus hominum seminare, atque principia fidei tradere. In qualibet enim facultate seminat, qui dat prima principia, secundum Origenem. Simul gaudeat, id est, cum electis et a se conversis in cœlo lætetur, et qui metit, id est, chorus Apostolorum et prædicatorum, qui homines ad fidem dispositos, ex doctrina Patriarcharum ac Prophetarum ad fidem catholicam et Christi gratiam suis sermonibus perduxerunt, etiam cum Patriarchis in cœlo exsultent.
paras.en: Or, *gathereth fruit*, that is, abundant merit reaching unto life everlasting, which is the end and the reward. For of all divine perfections the highest is to be God's fellow-worker in bringing men back to their beginning and last end, according to Dionysius. Of whose reward it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 12:3|they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity|Qui multos erudiunt ad justitiam, fulgebunt quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates]]. [[4:36|that both he that soweth|Ut et qui seminat]], that is, the choir of the holy Patriarchs and the ancient Prophets, who first began to sow the word of God in men's hearts and to hand on the first principles of faith (for in any art he sows who gives the first principles, according to Origen), [[4:36|may rejoice together|simul gaudeat]], that is, may be glad in heaven with the elect and those converted by him, [[4:36|and he that reapeth|et qui metit]], that is, the choir of the Apostles and preachers, who by their sermons brought men disposed to the faith by the teaching of the Patriarchs and Prophets to the catholic faith and the grace of Christ: that they too may exult in heaven with the Patriarchs.

paras.t: In hoc enim, hoc est in facto isto spiritualis messis, est. verbum verum, hoc est, verificatur et locum habet illud commune proverbium quo utebantur Judi, dicendo: quia, hoc est quod, alius est qui seminat, et alius est qui metit. Hoc dicebant de messe corporali, quando alius seminavit, sed alius fructum collegit. Quod et in spirituali messe interdum contingit, ut dictum est. Non tamen semper fit ita; imo, sicut in corporali messe sepe idem est seminator et messor seu fructus perceptor, sic in messe spirituali frequenter idem est qui seminat, inchoando ecognitionem fidei christianæ in aliquo, et qui metit, perducendo eum ad plenam conversionem. Sic enim gloriatur apostolus Paulus ad Romanos, se prædicasse Christum ubi ante non fuit annuntiatus, ne super alienum fundamentum fabricare videretur. Sed quantum ad Judæos, qui Moysen et Prophetas receperunt, et quantum ad Samaritanos Moysen recipientes, tenet verbum Christi: quia in illis priores Sancti seminaverunt, Apostoli vero messuerunt.
paras.en: [[4:37|For in this|In hoc enim]], that is, in this matter of the spiritual harvest, [[4:37|is the saying true|est verbum verum]], that is, there is verified and has place that common proverb which the Jews used, saying: [[4:37|That it is one man that soweth, and it is another that reapeth|quia, hoc est quod, alius est qui seminat, et alius est qui metit]], *that*, that is. This they said of the bodily harvest, when one man sowed but another gathered the fruit. And this sometimes happens in the spiritual harvest too, as has been said. Yet it is not always so; rather, as in the bodily harvest the sower and the reaper or receiver of the fruit are often the same, so in the spiritual harvest he who sows, by beginning the knowledge of the Christian faith in someone, is often the same as he who reaps, by bringing him to full conversion. For so the apostle Paul glories to the Romans that he preached Christ where he had not been named before, lest he should seem to build upon another man's foundation[[Rom 15:20||]]. But as to the Jews, who received Moses and the Prophets, and as to the Samaritans, who received Moses, Christ's word holds: since among them the earlier Saints sowed, and the Apostles reaped.

paras.t: Ego misi vos metere, hoc est ad fidem colligere, quod vos non laborastis, hoc est populum Judæorum, quem vestris prædicationibus, scripturis et laboribus, non disposuistis ad fidei receptionem. Alii laboraverunt, hoc est, prædicti seminatores, Patriarchæ ac vates, non sine labore populum Judæorum ad Christi receptionem præparaverunt, prænuntiando ejus adventum, docendo unius Dei cultum, et vitia populi exstirpando; et vos in labores eorum introistis, hoc est, populum ab illis Sanctis præparatum, cultum et doctum, convertistis. Quod dictum est pro toto tempore quo Apostoli in Judæa prædicaverunt. Non enim tot millia Judæorum convertissent et spiritualiter possedissent, nisi per scripturas Prophetarum ac Patriarcharum dispositi fuissent ad christiana fidei susceptionem. Unde et Petrus - in die Pentecostes allegando Joelem, convertit tria millia Judæorum. Postremo, quamvis prædicatio Apostolorum fuit messio respectu prædicationis præcedentium patrum, fuit tamen semen et seminatio per comparationem ad fidem et opera meritoria auditorum, et etiam quoad propriam remunerationem in patria, secundum quod dicit Apostolus: Qui seminat in " benedictionibus, de benedictionibus metet vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[4:38|I have sent you to reap|Ego misi vos metere]], that is, to gather into the faith, [[4:38|that in which you did not labour|quod vos non laborastis]], that is, the people of the Jews, whom you did not dispose to receive the faith by your preaching, writings and labours. [[4:38|Others have laboured|Alii laboraverunt]], that is, the sowers spoken of, the Patriarchs and prophets, not without labour prepared the people of the Jews to receive Christ, by foretelling his coming, teaching the worship of one God, and rooting out the vices of the people; [[4:38|and you have entered into their labours|et vos in labores eorum introistis]], that is, you have converted the people prepared, tilled and taught by those Saints. This was said for the whole time in which the Apostles preached in Judea. For they would not have converted so many thousands of the Jews and possessed them spiritually had they not been disposed by the writings of the Prophets and Patriarchs to receive the Christian faith. Hence Peter too, on the day of Pentecost, by citing Joel, converted three thousand Jews[[Acts 2:14||]][[Acts 2:41||]]. Lastly, though the preaching of the Apostles was a reaping in respect of the preaching of the fathers before them, it was yet seed and sowing in comparison with the faith and meritorious works of their hearers, and also as to their own reward in the fatherland, according to what the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 9:6|he who soweth in blessings shall also reap blessings|Qui seminat in benedictionibus, de benedictionibus metet]] [Denis adds: “life everlasting”][[Gal 6:8||]].

paras.t: Ex civitate autem illa, nomine Sichar, multi crediderunt in eum Samaritanorum, credentes quod esset Christus, propter verbum mulieris testimonium perhientis: Quia dixit mihi omnia quæcumque feci: quod non potuit fieri virtute humana. Quum venissent ergo ad illum Samaritani, rogaverunt eum ut ibi maneret in Sichar. Cupiebant enim plenius informari de fide a Christo. Et mansit ibi duos lies. Cur Christus qui cœpit facere et docere, ibi sic mansit inter Samaritanos lam diu, quum dixerit alibi, In civitates. Samaritanorum ne intraveritis? Dicendum, quod Christus legislator non fuit sub lege hæc generali. Ccepit autem facere et docere ea quæ ad præcepta spectant moralia. Item, quod modicum est, pro nihilo reputatur. Christus vero non fuit multum cum Samaritanis.
paras.en: [[4:39|Now of that city many of the Samaritans believed in him|Ex civitate autem illa, nomine Sichar, multi crediderunt in eum]], named Sichar, [[4:39|many of the Samaritans|Samaritanorum]], believing that he was the Christ, [[4:39|for the word of the woman giving testimony: He told me all things whatsoever I have done|propter verbum mulieris testimonium perhientis : Quia dixit mihi omnia quæcumque fecí]]: which could not have been done by human power. [[4:40|So when the Samaritans were come to him, they desired that he would tarry there|Quum venissent ergo ad illum Samaritani, rogaverunt eum ut ibi maneret]] in Sichar. For they longed to be more fully informed of the faith by Christ. [[4:40|And he abode there two days|Et mansit ibi duos dies]]. Why did Christ, who [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]], stay so long there among the Samaritans, when he said elsewhere: [[Matt 10:5|into the city of the Samaritans enter ye not|In civitates Samaritanorum ne intraveritis]]? It must be said that Christ the lawgiver was not under this general law. And he began to do and to teach the things that belong to the moral precepts. Again, what is little is reckoned as nothing; and Christ was not long with the Samaritans.

paras.t: Et multo plures ex Samaritanis crediderunt in eum, propler sermonem ejus, tanquam ob causam persuasoriam ad fidem aliquo modo inducentem. Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens: quia diffusa est gratia in labiis ejus. Propter sapientiam igitur relucentem in verbis Christi et efficacissimam eloquentiam ejus, crediderunt in eum. Nunquam enim sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquebatur.
paras.en: [[4:41|And many more believed in him, because of his own word|Et multo plures crediderunt in eum propter sermonem ejus]], of the Samaritans, as a persuasive cause leading them in some way to faith. For [[Matt 7:29|he was teaching them as one having power|Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens]]: since [[Ps 44:3|grace is poured abroad in thy lips|diffusa est gratia in labiis ejus]] [Denis: “in his lips”]. Because of the wisdom shining in Christ's words, then, and his most effective eloquence, they believed in him. For [[John 7:46|Never did man speak like this man|Nunquam enim sic locutus est homo]] [Denis: “Never did man speak as this man spoke”].

paras.t: Et mulieri Samaritanæ dicebant: Quia jam non propter tuam loquelam, id est testimonium oris tui, credimus, tanquam propter causam solam, sive præcipuam. Nihilo minus crediderunt etiam propter testimonium ejus, sed non propter hoc solum, aut principaliter. Ipsi enim audivimus, id est, audiendo verba ejus sapientissima eonsideravimus, et scimus, id est, certe cognoscimus. Quamvis enim major sit certitudo evidenti? in scientia quam in fide, tamen major est certitudo adherentie in fide quam in scientia. Fides quoque innititur certiori fundamento, videlicet increatæ et incommutabili veritati; scientia autem, naturali rationi, quæ frequenter decipitur. Quia hic est vere Salvator mundi, hoc est universalis redemptor totius generis humani. Noverant enim Samaritani ex libris Moysis, humanum genus a paradiso expulsum propter originale peccatum, a quo liberari indigebat per Christum.
paras.en: [[4:42|And they said to the woman|Et mulieri Samaritanæ dicebant]], the Samaritan woman: [[4:42|We now believe, not for thy saying|Quia jam non propter tuam loquelam credimus]], that is, the testimony of your mouth, as the only or the chief cause. None the less they believed also because of her testimony, but not because of it alone or chiefly. [[4:42|for we ourselves have heard him|Ipsi enim audivimus]], that is, by hearing his most wise words we have considered, [[4:42|and know|et scimus]], that is, we know for certain. For although the certainty of evidence is greater in knowledge than in faith, yet the certainty of adherence is greater in faith than in knowledge. Faith also rests on a surer foundation, namely the uncreated and unchangeable truth; but knowledge on natural reason, which is often deceived. [[4:42|that this is indeed the Saviour of the world|Quia hic est vere Salvator mundi]], that is, the universal redeemer of the whole human race. For the Samaritans knew from the books of Moses that the human race had been driven out of paradise because of original sin[[Gen 3:23||]], from which it needed to be delivered through Christ.

paras.t: Post duos autem dies quibus mansit cum Samaritanis in civitate Sichar, exiit inde, quia jam roborati erant in fide, et abiit in. Galilæam. Aliqui tamen dicunt quod divertit a Nazareth in qua erat conceptus, nutritus ac demoratus. Voluerunt enim eum concives sui præcipitare, ut dicit Lucas. Unde subjungitur: Ipse enim Jesus testimonium perhibuit, quia Propheta in sua patria honorem non habet. quasi dicat Evangelista, Ideo recessit: Nazareth, quia spreverunt eum contribules ipsius. Alii vero affirmant oppositum, et quod ait, Non est Propheta sine honore, referunt ad tempus præteritum, quando habitatores Nazareth spreverant eum, quoniam nondum viderant signa ejus, quæ postmodum in Jerusalem conspexerunt, sicut patebit.
paras.en: [[4:43|Now after two days|Post duos autem dies]] in which he stayed with the Samaritans in the city of Sichar, [[4:43|he departed thence|exiit inde]], since they were now strengthened in the faith, [[4:43|and went into Galilee|et abiit in Galilæam]]. Some, however, say that he turned aside from Nazareth, in which he had been conceived, brought up and had dwelt. For his fellow-citizens wished to cast him down headlong, as Luke says[[Luke 4:29||]]. Hence there is added: [[4:44|For Jesus himself gave testimony that a prophet hath no honour in his own country|Ipse enim Jesus testimonium perhibuit, quia Propheta in sua patria honorem non habet]]: as though the Evangelist said, This is why he went away from Nazareth, because his own kinsfolk despised him. Others, however, affirm the opposite, and refer what he says, *A prophet is not without honour*, to time past, when the inhabitants of Nazareth had despised him because they had not yet seen his signs, which they afterwards beheld in Jerusalem, as will appear.

paras.t: Porro, quod dicit, Non est Propheta, etc., Marcus plenius recitat hoc modo: Non est Propheta sine honore, nisi in domo sua, et in cognatione sua, et in patria sua. Quod non est intelligendum pro omni tempore et singulis compatriotis. Interdum enim Propheta seu alius quicumque excellens, a suis compatriotis contemnitur, et interdum ab eis honoratur: ut patet de Isaia, quem Jerosolymitæ tempore Ezechiæ honoraverunt, tempore vero Manasse spreverunt et occiderunt. Sed hoc universaliter verum est, quod conterranei atque concives communiter proniores sunt ad contemnendum Prophetam seu alium eminentem inter eos natum et conversatum, quam extranei. Quod certum est oriri ex superbia atque invidia: quoniam homines male ferunt, quod compares sui eis præferantur, et concipiunt excellentiam illorum quasi minorativam propriæ dignitatis, ita quod comparatione illorum viliores videntur et minus reputantur: de quo dolent, et ad detrahendum aut persequendum provocantur. Compatriotæ quoque melius sciunt mutuam imperfectionem quam alii, et ubertim convertunt oculum mentis ad considerandum alios secundum id quod erant tempore pueritiæ, vel quando eis non excellebant. Sed vera caritas exigit ut de perfectione et gratia compatriotarum, domesticorum et vicinorum, amplius gaudeamus, eosque, imo Deum in eis, puta in donis suis, veneremur.
paras.en: Further, what he says, *A prophet is not*, etc., Mark gives more fully in this way: [[Mark 6:4|A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and in his own house, and among his own kindred|non est propheta sine honore nisi in patria sua]] [Denis's order: “but in his own house, and among his own kindred, and in his own country”]. This is not to be understood for all time and of every one of his countrymen. For sometimes a Prophet, or any other excellent man, is despised by his countrymen, and sometimes honoured by them: as appears of Isaias, whom the people of Jerusalem honoured in the time of Ezechias[[4 Kings 19:1||]][[4 Kings 20:4||]], but despised and slew in the time of Manasses[[4 Kings 21:16||]]. But this is universally true, that people of the same land and city are commonly more prone to despise a Prophet, or another eminent man born and living among them, than strangers are. That this arises from pride and envy is certain: since men take it ill that their equals should be preferred to them, and regard their excellence as a lessening of their own dignity, so that by comparison with them they seem baser and are less esteemed; at this they grieve, and are provoked to detraction or persecution. Countrymen also know one another's imperfection better than others do, and readily turn the eye of the mind to considering others according to what they were in the time of childhood, or when they did not excel them. But true charity requires that we rejoice the more at the perfection and grace of our countrymen, household and neighbours, and honour them, or rather God in them, namely in his gifts.

paras.t: Quum ergo venisset Jesus in Galilæam patriam suam, exceperunt eum Galilæi cum honore. Cujus ratio subditur: quum omnia, vidissent quæ fecerat Jerosolymis in die festo, videlicet multa et magna miracula quæ fecit in Jerusalem in festo paschali, ut dictum est in Joanne. Propter qua credidit Nicodemus, et dixit: ? Nemo potest hæc signa facere quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum eo. Quomodo autem Galilæi viderunt hee signa, subjungitur: Et ipsi enim Galilæi venerant ad diem festum Paschæ, quando Jesus operatus est illa. Tenebantur enim pracipue in solennitate paschali oblationem facere in templo Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[4:45|And when he was come into Galilee, the Galileans received him|Quum ergo venisset Jesus in Galilæam patriam suam, exceperunt eum Galilæi]], his own country, with honour. The reason for this is added: [[4:45|having seen all the things he had done at Jerusalem on the festival day|quum omnia vidissent quæ fecerat Jerosolymis in die festo]], namely the many and great miracles which he did in Jerusalem at the paschal feast, as was said in John[[John 2:23||]]. Because of these Nicodemus believed and said: [[John 3:2|no man can do these signs which thou dost, unless God be with him|Nemo potest hæc signa facere que tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum eo]]. How the Galileans saw these signs is added: [[4:45|for they also went to the festival day|Et ipsi enim Galilæi venerant ad diem festum]], of the Pasch, when Jesus worked them. For they were bound above all at the paschal solemnity to make an offering in the temple at Jerusalem.

paras.t: Venit ergo Jesus iterum in Cana villa Galilææ provinciæ, ubi fecit aquam vinum, ut dictum est secundo capitulo. Secundum Augustinum et Bedam, Galilæi acceperunt Jesum cum honore quodam superfieiali, non ex dilectione vel fide, sed curiositate, propter signa prædicta; alii tamen aliter sentiunt.
paras.en: [[4:46|He came again therefore into Cana of Galilee|Venit ergo Jesus iterum in Cana villa Galilææ]], the village of the province of Galilee, [[4:46|where he made the water wine|ubi fecit aquam vinum]], as was said in the second chapter. According to Augustine and Bede, the Galileans received Jesus with a certain superficial honour, not out of love or faith, but out of curiosity, because of the signs spoken of; others, however, think otherwise.

4.title: Prosecutio expositionis hujus capituli quarti, ab eo loco quo dicitur: Et erat quidam regulus, cujus filius infirmabatur.
4.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this fourth chapter, from the place where it is said: “And there was a certain ruler, whose son was sick.”

paras.t: Et erat quidam regulus, cujus filius infirmabatur Capharnaum. In hac enim civitate, quæ fuit metropolis Galilææ, habitavit regulus iste cum filio suo febricitante. Denique, secundum Bedam, regulus iste vocatur diminutive, quasi parvus rex. Chrysostomus vero dicit, quod non erat parvus rex, sed regulus nominatur, quoniam regis stirpis erat. Alii dicunt, quod vocatur regulus, quia officialis erat Cæsaris, deputatus ad custodiam urbis Capharnaum. Quos sequitur quidam, reprobans dictum Bedæ, per hoc quod Romani volentes frangere superbiam Judæorum, abstulerunt eis regiam dignitatem, ita quod pro tunc nullus rex fuit in Judæa. Sed istud non videtur resolutum. Herodes enim, sub quo natus est Jesus, qui occidit infantes, rex fuit, ut dicitur in Matthæo; similiter Herodes qui decollavit Joannem, sub quo passus est Christus, dicitur rex apud Matthæum et Marcum. Et tamen regnaverunt in Judæa. Quemadmodum ergo nominati sunt reges, sic iste regulus dici posset. Abstulerunt autem Romani regiam dignitatem a Judæis, quantum ad hoc quod nullus de semine eorum regnavit, sed alienigenæ. Romani quoque jusserunt ut sine eorum consensu nullus assumeret nomen regis. Propter quod infra habetur: Omnis qui se regem facit, contradicit Cæsari. Quidquid autem horum dicatur, certum est quod regulus iste fuit excellens persona, unus de principalioribus terræ.
paras.en: [[4:46|And there was a certain ruler, whose son was sick at Capharnaum|Et erat quidam regulus, cujus filius infirmabatur Capharnaum]]. For in this city, which was the chief city of Galilee, this ruler lived with his son, who was sick of a fever. Now according to Bede this man is called by a diminutive *regulus* [“little king”; the Douay-Rheims has “ruler”], as though a petty king. Chrysostom, however, says that he was not a petty king, but is named *regulus* because he was of royal stock. Others say he is called *regulus* because he was an officer of Cæsar, appointed to guard the city of Capharnaum. One writer follows these, rejecting Bede's saying on the ground that the Romans, wishing to break the pride of the Jews, had taken the royal dignity from them, so that at that time there was no king in Judæa. But this does not seem to settle the matter. For Herod, under whom Jesus was born, who killed the infants, was king, as is said in Matthew[[Matt 2:1||]][[Matt 2:16||]]; likewise Herod who beheaded John[[Mark 6:16||]], under whom Christ suffered[[Luke 23:7||]], is called king in Matthew and Mark[[Matt 14:9||]][[Mark 6:14||]][[Mark 6:26||]]. And yet they reigned in Judæa. As, then, they were named kings, so this man could be called a little king. But the Romans took the royal dignity from the Jews in this respect, that none of their own seed reigned, but foreigners. The Romans also ordered that no one should take the name of king without their consent. That is why it is said further on: [[John 19:12|whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar|Omnis qui se regem facit, contradicit Cæsari]]. But whichever of these is said, it is certain that this ruler was a person of standing, one of the chief men of the land.

paras.t: Hic regulus quum audisset quod Jesus adveniret a Judæa, per Samariam, in Galilæam. Jam enim famosus factus fuit Jesus propter miracula sua, et propter Baptismum quo per se et per discipulos baptizavit, itemque propter Joannis Baptistæ testificationem: ideo fama ejus præcurrebat eum. Unde in Matthæo legitur, quia abiit opinio ejus in totam Syriam: quæ utique fuit grande regnum. Abiit ad eum in Cana Galilææ, ubi reperit Christum, et rogabat eum ut descenderet in Capharnaum, quæ fuit in situ bassiori quam Cana, et sanaret filium ejus, quem putavit non posse sanari a Christo, nisi corporaliter præsente. Nondum enim agnovit Jesum esse verum Deum ubique præsentem, et quod angeli sancti ejus essent ministri, quorum ministerio potuit omnes ægros curare.
